original_question: For the split properties in Figure 5, does Split(Omega,T) imply Split(T,Gamma)?
target_in_paper: §8, Problem 8.1(1) (“Splittability”), the first question attached to Figure 5: whether Split(Ω, T) implies Split(T, Γ). ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the exact implication asked in the paper’s official problem statement, and it correctly ties it to Figure 5 and the splittability notation. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
missing_details: The quantifier over spaces is implicit in the draft: in this chapter, the standing scope is sets of real numbers, so the question is whether every set of reals X with Split(Ω, T) also has Split(T, Γ). ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

The draft does not say that the relevant covers are open covers, and that throughout this discussion a “cover” is nontrivial, meaning X itself is not a member of the cover. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

Split(A, B) is not defined: the paper defines it by requiring that every cover 𝒰 in A can be partitioned into two disjoint subcovers 𝒱 and 𝒲, each containing a subfamily that is a member of B. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

The symbols Ω, T, and Γ are left undefined in the draft: Ω is the family of open ω-covers, T is the family of open τ-covers, and Γ is the family of open γ-covers. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

The definition of a τ-cover is missing: a τ-cover is a large open cover 𝒰 such that for each x, y in X, either {U in 𝒰 : x in U and y not in U} is finite, or {U in 𝒰 : y in U and x not in U} is finite; here “large” means that each x in X belongs to infinitely many members of 𝒰. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))

The draft does not unpack ω-cover and γ-cover: an ω-cover covers every finite subset of X inside some member, while a γ-cover is infinite and each point of X belongs to all but finitely many members. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
refined_question: For a set of real numbers X, where a cover means an open cover of X with X not itself a member, let Ω be the family of open ω-covers of X, Γ the family of open γ-covers of X, and T the family of open τ-covers of X (that is, large open covers 𝒰 such that for every x, y in X, either {U in 𝒰 : x in U and y not in U} is finite or {U in 𝒰 : y in U and x not in U} is finite). If Split(A, B) denotes the property that every cover 𝒰 in A can be partitioned into two disjoint subcovers 𝒱 and 𝒲, each containing a subfamily that is a member of B, must Split(Ω, T) imply Split(T, Γ)? ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
justification: The draft is already aimed at the exact first clause of the paper’s official open problem on splittability, namely Problem 8.1(1) in §8. What it lacks is not a change of mathematical target but the local context that makes the problem stand alone: the chapter’s ambient scope of sets of reals, the section-8 definition of Split(A, B), and the section-7.1 definitions of large, ω-, τ-, and γ-covers, including Γ ⊆ T ⊆ Ω. Adding precisely those ingredients yields a faithful standalone version without broadening the problem. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
